lead: libewf is a library for the Expert Witness (EWF) image format, with command-line tools to create, check, inspect, export and mount E01 images. Many other forensic programs use it to read these images.
use_when: You need to create an E01 image from a drive on Linux.
You want to verify an E01 image or read its case details.
You need to convert an E01 image to a raw image, or the other way round.
You want to mount an E01 image on Linux to look inside.

features.title: Tools in the package
items: ewfacquire writes data from devices and files to EWF files
ewfacquirestream writes data from standard input to EWF files
ewfverify checks the media data in EWF files
ewfinfo shows the information stored in EWF files

features.title: Convert and mount
items: ewfexport exports to split raw format or to another EWF version
ewfmount mounts EWF files with FUSE
ewfrecover makes a new EWF set from a damaged one

features.title: Acquisition settings
items: Records case number, evidence number, description, examiner and notes
Adds SHA-1 or SHA-256 next to MD5
Sets compression, segment size and format
Can retry read errors and write a log file

features.title: Library features
items: Reads and writes SMART and EnCase formats, including E01
Reads logical evidence files L01 and Lx01
Supports delta (shadow) files and resuming a write

requirements: Linux, macOS and other Unix-like systems. Many Linux systems have a package named ewf-tools. To build from source, follow the build guide on the project wiki. ewfmount needs FUSE.

steps.title: Install the tools
steps.text: On a Debian-based system, install the ewf-tools package. If you build from source, follow the project's building guide on its wiki. Run any tool with -h to see its help.

steps.title: Protect the source drive
steps.text: Connect the evidence drive through a write blocker and find its device name. Device names such as /dev/sdb are only examples, so confirm the right one first.

steps.title: Acquire an E01 image
steps.text: Run ewfacquire with the source device. It asks questions about case number, examiner, evidence number, description, format, compression and segment size, then it starts. The -t option sets the output name without extension.

steps.title: Check the details
steps.text: Use ewfinfo to see the stored case details and the hash values. Compare the hash with the one shown at the end of the acquisition.

steps.title: Verify the image
steps.text: ewfverify reads the segments again and checks the stored hash. Add -d sha256 to calculate an extra SHA-256 value. -l writes the result to a log file.

steps.title: Export or mount
steps.text: To make a raw copy, use ewfexport with -f raw and -t for the output name. To look inside the image, use ewfmount with the first segment and an empty folder as the mount point.

steps.title: Work from the raw view
steps.text: The mount point shows the data of the image as a raw view. Tools such as the Sleuth Kit can read it. Unmount the folder when you finish.

options.what: Sets the output file name without extension. The default is image.
Records case number, examiner name, evidence number, description and notes.
Calculates an extra digest besides MD5. sha1 and sha256 are the choices.
Chooses the EWF format. The default is encase6.
Writes verification errors and the digest to a log file.
Exports to raw format. Raw is the default format of ewfexport.
Shows the information in DFXML instead of plain text.

cases.title: Creating E01 images on Linux
cases.why: ewfacquire stores case details, compression and hashes in an image that other forensic tools can open.

cases.title: Checking evidence integrity
cases.why: ewfverify re-reads the image and checks the stored hashes, which is useful when you receive an image from another lab.

cases.title: Converting between formats
cases.why: ewfexport changes an E01 image to raw so tools that cannot read E01 can process it.

cases.title: Quick look inside an image
cases.why: ewfmount gives a raw view that standard Linux tools can read without making a full copy.

cases.title: Damaged image files
cases.why: ewfrecover tries to make a new EWF set from a damaged one.

strengths: Open source under the LGPL, used as a base by other forensic programs.
Separate small tools for each job: acquire, verify, inspect, export, mount.
Reads and writes the common E01 and Ex01 formats.
Records case details and hashes inside the image.
limits: The project calls the library experimental. Test your results with a second tool.
For Ex01, the project says bzip2 compression is still in progress and encryption is not supported.
L01 and Lx01 logical evidence files can be read but not written.
ewfacquire does not block writes to the source. Use a write blocker.
These are command-line tools, so beginners need practice with device names and options.
No analysis is included. You need another tool to examine the contents.

works_with.note: Also writes E01 images with a graphical interface
Make a raw image first, then convert it
Reads E01 images with libewf support
